## Topics

### Geocentric vs. Heliocentric Solar System Models
A historical survey of astronomical models from Aristotle's Earth-centered universe through Aristarchus, Ptolemy, Copernicus, Kepler, Galileo, and Newton, tracing the 2,000-year struggle to establish heliocentrism.
*_(~45% of transcript; Sections 9-20)_*

### Paradigm Shifts in Science
Examination of how long it can take for a dominant scientific model to be overturned, using the geocentric-to-heliocentric transition as the central case study and drawing implications for the future of Bowen Family Systems Theory.
*_(~10% of transcript; Sections 2-3, 12)_*

### Differentiation of Self and Emotional Objectivity
Presentation of the equation DOS = EO + A (Differentiation of Self equals Emotional Objectivity plus Action), with emphasis on emotional neutrality as the mechanism enabling non-reactive engagement and boundary maintenance.
*_(~10% of transcript; Sections 4-5)_*

### Religious and Institutional Resistance to Scientific Change
Discussion of how the Catholic Church and Jesuits opposed heliocentrism on theological grounds, leading to Galileo's trial by the Inquisition and house arrest.
*_(~8% of transcript; Sections 14-15, 18)_*

### Physical-to-Biological Continuity in Bowen Theory
The presenter's argument that early physical evolution on Earth carries over into biological functioning, and that broadening perspective from family to cosmos contributes to emotional objectivity.
*_(~10% of transcript; Sections 6-8)_*

### Newton's Theory of Universal Gravitation and Forces
Description of Newton's introduction of gravitational force as an explanatory mechanism for Kepler's laws of planetary motion, with a note that forces are central to Bowen theory but underused in biology.
*_(~8% of transcript; Sections 19-20)_*

### Brain Functioning and Differentiation of Self
Brief introduction to a forthcoming technical presentation on neurological processes related to differentiation of self, described as the second mini-lecture of the session.
*_(~5% of transcript; Section 3)_*
